answers.reasoning: The p289 J has3rows and2columns, so a two-sided inverse cannot exist. Page291 supplies a2×3 pseudoinverse with stated rank assumptions. Negative entries or scalar input components do not settle invertibility.

Matrix multiplication J(3×2)pdot(2×1) yields qdot(3×1), so forward flow is pdot→J→qdot. J^T onpdot is dimensionally invalid and the printed qdot→J→pdot reverses input/output. J+ maps task rates to wheel rates, not task rates to task rates.

Full column rank makes J^TJ a positive-definite n×n matrix. Its inverse followed byJ^T gives an n×m pseudoinverse; JJ^T has rankn<m and is not invertible. A rectangular ordinary inverse does not exist; J^TJ alone has wrong shape and action.

Full row rank makes JJ^T a positive-definite m×m matrix, giving n×m J+=J^T(JJ^T)^−1. J^TJ has rankm<n and is singular. Transpose alone works only under extra row-orthonormality, not every full-row-rankJ.
If some nonzeroz satisfiesJz=0, thenJ^TJz=0, proving the Gram matrix singular. Thus the shortcut with ordinary inverse fails; the Moore–Penrose pseudoinverse remains definable, for example via SVD.
